unreachable.reason: The two points are COVP-012 (A handshakes in two consecutive cycles) and COVP-013 (two or more accepted requests not yet answered). Both need the device to accept a new request while the previous response is still pending. Only the device drives a_ready (GP-4.1-01: TL-UL device interface). The host must hold a request with the same fields until a_ready=1 (GP-4.1-04, CHK-011(a)), and the test bench may not assume a_ready=1 (GP-10-26 / D-014). So no legal stimulus can force a second acceptance. The gpio register interface takes a new request only after the D handshake of the previous one: a_ready is low while a response is pending. The tests already do what would otherwise hit these points. CHK-038 and the random regression keep i_a_valid high back-to-back with zero or random 0-2 cycle gaps, use distinct a_source values, and run 1700+ requests with long stretches of i_d_ready=1. Neither point was hit, which shows the device never accepts in consecutive cycles and never holds two requests. Reset cannot make a stale entry count either: D-016 (GP-10-31/GP-10-32) discards a response pending at reset, so the outstanding count is cleared at reset. CHK-030 accepts a Get under back-pressure, resets, and then sends new requests, and that did not hit COVP-013. A request with i_a_intg_flip=1 still gets at most one response through the same single-request flow control, so it cannot create a second outstanding request. The only way to reach these points would be a device that accepts requests before answering earlier ones, and this design does not do that.
